Speaker's Card/Request to Speak:
If you would like to address the City Council/Board of Directors on a scheduled agenda item - including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments - please complete the Request to Speak Form. The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The Request to Speak Form assists the Mayor/Chair in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council/Board of Directors are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council/Board minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council/Board of Directors. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor/Chair), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that
the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor/Chair or the City Council/Board of Directors during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. Regular Orange County Great Park Board meetings are broadcast live every 4th Tuesday of the month at 2 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 2 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting), Wednesdays at 8 a.m., Thursdays at 7 p.m., and Saturdays at 7 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting) until the next Orange County Great Park Board meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council/Successor Agency meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the Clerk of the Board/City Clerkâ€™s office at (949) 724-6205.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Great Park Board meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org and the Orange County Great Park website at ocgp.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Orange County Great Park Board meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Regular meetings of the Orange County Great Park Board are held on the fourth Tuesday of each month at 2:00 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations:

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:11 p.m. on June
11, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Michael C. Carroll
  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor:  Christina Shea
 City Council/Great Park Minutes  June 11, 2019

  1.  CLOSED SESSION

  1.1  * CLOSED SESSION ITEM NO. 1.1 HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE
  AGENDA ORIGINALLY POSTED ON MAY 30, 2019

  Due to the removal of the Closed Session item, Mayor Shea reordered the
  agenda as follows:

  Presentations 2.1 and 2.2
  Consent Calendar
  Public Hearing Item 4.1
  Council Business Items 6.1 and 6.2
  Public Hearing Item 5.1
  Council Business Item 6.3

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Members of Boy Scout Troop 616 lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Cody Adams from Free Chapel Orange County Church in Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  MOMENT OF SILENCE

  Mayor Shea asked for a moment of silence for the victims of the City of Virginia Beach in
  the wake of the tragic shooting that took place on Friday, May 31.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Proclaim June 17-23, 2019 as Public Safety's "Amateur Radio Week"

  Mayor Shea introduced Commander Michael Kent, Emergency
  Management Administrator Bobby Simmons, Sergeant Jasper Kim, and
  members of the Irvine Disaster Emergency Communications team, and
  presented a proclamation recognizing June 17-23, 2019 as “Amateur Radio
  Week.”

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council/Great Park Minutes  June 11, 2019

  2.2  Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee Annual Report

  Mayor Shea introduced Tina Anderson, President of the Irvine 2/11 Marine
  Adoption Committee, who presented the Committee’s annual report.
  Lieutenant Colonel Caleb Hyatt, 2/11 Marines, also expressed his
  appreciation to the City Council for its support on behalf of the Irvine 2/1
  Marines.

  City Council discussion included: acknowledging Ms. Anderson for her
  recognition by the State legislature as “Woman of the Year”; and inquired
  about the upcoming Car Wash fundraiser at Lakeview Senior Center on
  Saturday, June 22.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo noted two recent near-drowning incidents that took place over
  the weekend and reminded residents to be diligent about water safety, with information
  available on the City’s website at cityofirvine.org; and this past weekend, the 73rd annual
  Antoinette Perry (“Tony”) Awards for excellence in theater were presented on the east
  coast, with one of the recipients being Rachel Hauck, the daughter of former employee
  Connie Hauck, who won a Tony award for best set design for a musical.

  Councilmember Khan, as Chairwoman of the Orange County Great Park Board, invited
  the community to the grand opening of the Upper Bee and Bosque areas at the Orange
  County Great Park on Saturday, June 15 at 7 a.m., and encouraged visitors to sign up to
  participate in the longest “high-five” chain by signing up individually or as a group at
  highfiveirvine.com; and expressed her appreciation to DARE officers for their dedication
  to the DARE program and the children who participate.

  Councilmember Carroll provided a brief report on his attendance at the recent Southern
  California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting and some of the items
  discussed, including an amendment to the Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  (RHNA) report, a scholarship and intern program, and audit findings from CalTrans
  reflecting accounting deficiencies in which Councilmember Carroll, as the City’s
  representative to SCAG, will represent the City of Irvine on the audit committee.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council/Great Park Minutes  June 11, 2019

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

    The City’s Human Resources & Innovation Department recently launched
  Showcase & Shadow Week, a new employee engagement program that gives our
  City’s leadership team a deeper level of appreciation for the behind-the-scenes
  work employees achieve on a daily basis to serve the Irvine community. This
  year’s program paired upper management with operational staff from Public
  Works, Community Services, and Public Safety for half a day. The program is also
  designed to help develop a more engaged and dedicated workforce.

    As part of the City’s efforts to raise awareness for drowning prevention, the City’s
  largest group swim lesson will take place on Friday, June 21 at 5:30 p.m. at the
  William Woollett Jr. Aquatics Center, followed by recreation swim, activities,
  games, and a screening of the movie Trolls at dusk. Adults and children of all
  swimming abilities are invited to participate in the free event.

    The popular Movies on the Lawn series begins Friday, June 21 at the Orange
  County Great Park. Movies will be shown throughout June and July, with classic
  films like Meet Me in St. Louis, showing on Fridays, and blockbuster hits like How
  to Train Your Dragon on the big screen on Saturdays.

    June is National Safety Month, and to help take steps to stay safe, the Irvine
  Police Department will provide training designed to educate parents on the risk
  associated with use of the internet an social media platforms by our youth.
  Attendees will be provided with information and tools to assist in mitigating the risk
  of children and teens being exposed to dangerous individuals and content. Details
  are available on the City’s website at cityofirvine.org.

    The City of Irvine was recently recognized for excellence for the Community
  Emergency Response Team (CERT) program and Irvine Community Television
  (ICTV) programming. The CERT team received an award for creating the CERT
  class taught in Mandarin, and was recognized at the 2019 California for All CERT
  and Listos Preparedness Conference for the program, which is the first of its kind
  in the state and is believed to be the first in the nation. The ICTV team was
  presented with an award of distinction for Best Event Video from the California

  through City policy; confirmed that the 45-day rule for the displaying of

  parties.
